AIICO Insurance Plc grew insurance revenue by 14.7 per cent to N114.57 billion in the nine months ended 30 September 2026, while gross premium written rose 5.9 per cent to N163.58 billion from N153.40 billion.
The Group in its unaudited results showed profit before tax rose 27.3 per cent to N19.42 billion from N15.25 billion, while profit after tax increased 25.6 per cent to N17.28 billion from N13.75 billion. Earnings per share increased to 47 kobo from 37 kobo.
Profit before tax excluding unrealised foreign exchange effects rose even faster, up 35.3 per cent to N21.46 billion from N15.86 billion. Profit after tax excluding unrealised FX effects rose 21.4 per cent to N19.05 billion.
Net insurance service result improved 10.4 per cent to N9.45 billion from N8.56 billion, though net insurance service margin eased slightly to 8.30 per cent from 8.60 per cent. Net insurance and investment result surged 47.4 per cent to N36.87 billion from N25.02 billion, reflecting stronger investment performance alongside underwriting.
Life business grew 23.2 per cent year-to-date to N42.23 billion from N34.28 billion at 31 December 2025. The Group wrote N8.5 billion of new-business CSM in the period.
Group Life net combined ratio improved sharply to 73 per cent from 100 per cent, a 27 percentage point improvement, indicating stronger underwriting discipline. Non-Life net combined ratio, however, weakened to 107 per cent from 92 per cent, as claims pressures weighed on that segment.
Total equity rose 14.9 per cent to N113.33 billion from N98.67 billion at 31 December 2025, while total assets grew 21.3 per cent to N708.29 billion from N584.06 billion. Solvency ratio on a regulatory basis improved to 347 per cent from 329 per cent, well above regulatory minimums.
Speaking on the performance, the managing director and chief executive officer, AIICO Insurance, Babatunde Fajemirokun stated that “with recapitalisation complete, competition will be won on underwriting discipline and capital efficiency, not premium volume.”
He added that AIICO met the new requirements without raising capital, grew profit before tax by 2 5 per cent and added N8.5 billion of future Life profit this year, saying that the Non -Life faced a tough market, but our diversified model carried the Group, and we are acting on Non -Life costs and pricing.”
The Chief Financial Officer, AIICO Insurance, Mrs. Bisola Elias, said, “we have always focused on the measures that drive shareholder value and are now emphasizing this focus .
“PAT excluding unrealised FX rose 2 1.4 per cent to N19.0 billion, and the Life CSM grew 23.2% to N42.2 billion, with new business adding future profit faster than we release it. ROE of 21 per cent reflects a 15 per cent larger equity base, which we are focused on deploying at attractive returns.”
